What I read: the request JSON with the script, the 03/05 boundary context and the first-reading record, then source/original.txt, reading-flow/page-04.json and storyboard-r16-04.json (the previous pass). I read the script before opening the images.

Images I opened with Read and looked at: storyboards-unnumbered/page-04.png, storyboards/page-04.png (numbered PNG; the request hashes the SVG), review/page-03.png, review/page-04.png and review/page-05.png. I did not open assets/panels/04-3.png separately. I judged it from the composed preview.

Unnumbered PNG: a wide top panel and two tall panels below. Order: 'Soon, his slot comes up.', then 'NOW · A-12'; then 'A quick vitals check first.', then the nurse's balloon 'Hi, Ravi! Just relax your arm for me.' with its tail down to the nurse; then 'Dr. Ananya is notified when he's ready.', then the label 'RAVI ·' / 'READY' at the lower right of the panel. The numbered PNG gives the same order.

The change since r16 (04-3 label): the text is the same, 'RAVI · READY', now wrapped as 'RAVI ·' / 'READY'. In review/page-04.png it sits on the tablet's notification card, below the check-mark icon, so it clearly reads as on-screen text. Both of Ananya's hands stay visible: the left fingers on the tablet edge to the left of the label and the right fingers on the right edge. The label does not reach her face or stethoscope.

Minor note, not blocking: the wrap leaves the separator dot dangling at the end of the first line ('RAVI ·'). It is still read as one label, and the same text is verbatim from source PAGE 4. Moving the dot to the second line could be considered at lettering, but the separator is legitimate as it stands.

04-1 preview: the two blue chairs at Ravi's right are empty, which is the recorded edit. Ravi is standing with his bag on his left shoulder and his right hand at his trouser pocket, looking up at the TV, and 'NOW · A-12' sits on the screen. Meera types at reception at the right, and the label sits above her head without touching it. Two figures seen from behind and a QR stand at the left remain. A vitals cart beside reception sets up 04-2.

04-2 preview: Ravi is seated with the cuff on his left upper arm, the oximeter on his finger and the watch on that wrist, with his bag on the floor. The nurse in lavender scrubs holds the bulb, and the monitor shows only an abstract wave. The balloon is above her head and its tail ends at her hair. It does not cover either face, the cuff arm or the bulb hand. The reception counter edge and a teal chair are visible behind her.
04-3 preview: consultation room with a window, a plant and a closed laptop at the lower right. Ananya looks down at the tablet with a small smile.
Script against source: both captions, both labels and the nurse's line are verbatim from source PAGE 4.

04-1: the automatic warning (step 1 to 2) is a same-row move from the caption at top-left to the TV label at top-right. Ravi stands between them looking up and right at the TV, so his gaze carries the eye forward.
04-2: the caption leads to the single balloon and its tail leads down to the nurse. Ravi's smile at the lower left is the silent response. Only one balloon, so there is no proximity confusion.

04-3: the caption at the top leads down through Ananya's lowered gaze to the label on the tablet, about 580 px below. Her eye line bridges the gap, so the tall panel reads downward without stalling. With the label now on the card, the panel exits at the lower right of the page toward page 05.

transitions.observation: Same waiting area, TV and blue chairs. The two chairs where Raman and Priya sat are now empty, and Ravi stands under 'NOW · A-12' with his bag back on his shoulder, putting his phone away. 'Soon, his slot comes up' gives the short time skip.

From the waiting area to the vitals corner beside reception. The vitals cart seen next to reception in 04-1, the counter and teal chair behind the nurse, and the caption 'A quick vitals check first.' carry the move. The skipped walk is covered by 'first'.

Cut to a different room: window, plant, desk and closed laptop, with Ananya alone with her tablet. The caption gives the cause, 'notified when he's ready', meaning after the vitals check, and the tablet card shows what she sees. The left-to-right placement puts it after the vitals.

From review/page-05.png: the same room (window with plants, closed laptop on the desk) and the same white coat and teal kurta. The tablet is no longer visible. Ravi now sits in the patient chair with his bag on the floor, and Ananya greets him by name, so the notification visibly leads to the meeting.

readingReview.comparison:
My image-only order matches the first reader's and the script.
(1) Labels not visibly on screens in the storyboard: resolved by the art. 'NOW · A-12' sits on the wall TV and 'RAVI · READY' on the tablet's notification card. The A-12 label sits above Meera's head and does not touch her.
(2) Jumps rely on captions: the art adds the setting cues (counter and teal chair in 04-2; window, plant, laptop and desk in 04-3). Acceptable.
(3) Empty lower halves and the break after the dot: the art fills both tall panels. The 'RAVI ·' break is a minor cosmetic point that does not affect reading. Noted above as optional for lettering.
No unresolved items.
